info.name: RequestHub API
info.description:
# RequestHub API

REST API of the RequestHub service request management system (Node.js, Express 5, MongoDB). USERs submit and track their own service requests; ADMINs review every request and move it through the status workflow.

## Base URL

All requests use the collection variable `{{baseUrl}}`, which defaults to `http://localhost:5000/api` (the backend's default `PORT=5000` plus the `/api` prefix mounted in `src/app.js`).

## Authentication: HttpOnly cookies (no Bearer token)

The API does **not** use an `Authorization` header. `POST /auth/login` (and `POST /auth/refresh`) respond with two `Set-Cookie` headers:

| Cookie | Lifetime (default) | Path | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accessToken` | 15 minutes (`ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_MINUTES`) | `/` | every protected endpoint |
| `refreshToken` | 7 days (`REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS`) | `/api/auth` | only `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/logout` |

Both are `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (plus `Secure` when `NODE_ENV=production`). Tokens never appear in response bodies.

**Postman handles this automatically:** its cookie jar stores the cookies from the login response and sends them with every later request to `localhost`, respecting each cookie's path. No auth configuration is needed; this collection is set to *No Auth* on purpose. Open **Cookies** (under the Send button) to inspect or delete them.

The cookie jar holds **one session at a time**: running *Login (ADMIN)* replaces the USER's cookies and vice versa. Log in with the role that the endpoint needs before calling it.

When the access token expires (after 15 minutes), protected calls return `401`; run **Authentication › Refresh** (or log in again).

## Roles

- `USER`: created by public registration. Creates, lists, views, edits and cancels **their own** requests.
- `ADMIN`: cannot be registered through the API; create one with `npm run seed:admin` in `backend/` (uses `SEED_ADMIN_*` from `backend/.env`). Lists and views **all** requests, changes their status and lists users. An ADMIN **cannot** create, edit or cancel requests (`403`).

The role is read from the database on every request, never from the token.

## Response shapes

| Kind | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| Single resource | `{ "success": true, "message"?: "...", "data": { "<name>": { ... } } }` |
| List | `{ "success": true, "data": [ ... ], "pagination"?: { ... } }` (only `GET /requests` paginates) |
| Action | `{ "success": true, "message": "..." }` |
| Error | `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errors"?: { "<field>": "..." } }` |

With `NODE_ENV=development` error responses also contain a `stack` field (omitted from the examples here).

Users are serialised with `id` (no `_id`, `__v` or password hash). Service requests are serialised with MongoDB's `_id` and `__v`.

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning in this API | Typical message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Validation failed (body or query), malformed JSON, or `:id` is not a valid MongoDB ObjectId | `Validation failed` (+ `errors` per field), `At least one field is required`, `Malformed JSON`, `Invalid ID` |
| `401` | **Authentication** failed: no `accessToken` cookie, invalid/expired token, revoked session, deleted user, or bad login credentials | `Authentication required`, `Invalid or expired access token`, `Session is no longer valid`, `Invalid email or password` |
| `403` | **Authorization** failed: logged in, but the role may not call this endpoint (e.g. ADMIN creating a request, USER changing a status) | `You do not have permission to perform this action` |
| `404` | The request does not exist **or belongs to another USER** (ownership is hidden, never reported as 403); also unknown routes | `Request not found`, `Route not found: <METHOD> <path>` |
| `409` | **Business-rule conflict**: editing a non-`PENDING` request, a status change not allowed by the workflow, or an already-registered email | `Only pending requests can be edited`, `Cannot change status from X to Y`, `Email is already registered` |
| `413` | JSON body larger than 10 kB | `Request body too large` |
| `500` | Unexpected server error (details are logged, never returned) | `Internal server error` |

For service request endpoints the checks run in this order: logged in (`401`) → role (`403`) → body/query validation (`400`) → id format (`400 Invalid ID`) and existence/ownership (`404`) → status rules (`409`).

## Status workflow

```
PENDING ──► IN_PROGRESS ──► RESOLVED   (final)
   │             │
   └─────────────┴────────► CANCELLED  (final)
```

| From | Allowed next statuses |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | `IN_PROGRESS`, `CANCELLED` |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `RESOLVED` | none (final) |
| `CANCELLED` | none (final) |

Any other change, including a "change" to the same status (e.g. `PENDING` → `PENDING`), returns `409 Cannot change status from X to Y`.

## Collection variables

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | API root, default `http://localhost:5000/api` |
| `userName`, `userEmail`, `userPassword` | Account used by *Register* and *Login (USER)* |
| `adminEmail`, `adminPassword` | Seeded admin account used by *Login (ADMIN)*. **Set these to your `SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.** |
| `userId` | Set automatically from *Register* / *Login (USER)*. For reference only (compare with `createdBy`); no endpoint takes a user id. |
| `requestId` | Set automatically by *Create request*; used by every `/requests/:id` call. |

## Suggested walkthrough

1. **Health › Health check**: confirm the API is up.
2. **Authentication › Register** (once), then **Login (USER)**, then **Get current user**.
3. **Service Requests › Create request** (stores `requestId`), **List requests**, **Get request by ID**, **Update request**.
4. **Authentication › Login (ADMIN)**, then **Service Requests › Update request status (ADMIN)** (`IN_PROGRESS`, then `RESOLVED`), and **Users / Admin › List users**.
5. To try **Cancel request**, log in as the USER again and create a fresh request first (a `RESOLVED` or `CANCELLED` request cannot be cancelled).
6. **Authentication › Logout**.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
Registration, cookie-based login, session refresh and logout (`/api/auth`).

- **Register** creates a `USER` account only; it does **not** log in and sets no cookies.
- **Login** sets the `accessToken` (path `/`) and `refreshToken` (path `/api/auth`) HttpOnly cookies. Postman's cookie jar stores them and sends them automatically.
- **Refresh** rotates the session: the old refresh token stops working and new cookies are set.
- **Logout** revokes the session and clears both cookies. It never fails.

Request bodies are JSON. Unknown fields (for example `role`) are ignored.

request.description:
Creates a new **USER** account.

**Authentication:** none (public). **Role:** none.

**Body (JSON)**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | 2–50 characters after trimming |
| `email` | string | yes | Valid email (`x@y.z`); trimmed and lower-cased; must not already be registered (case-insensitive) |
| `password` | string | yes | 8–72 characters (max 72 **bytes**, the bcrypt limit) |

A `role` field is ignored: public registration always creates a `USER`. Admins are created only with `npm run seed:admin`.

Registration does **not** log the user in and sets **no** cookies. Run *Login (USER)* next.

**Script:** stores `data.user.id` in `{{userId}}`.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201` | Account created |
| `400` | `Validation failed`, `errors` lists each invalid field |
| `409` | `Email is already registered` (re-running this request with the same `userEmail` gives 409; change the variable) |

response.name: 400 Validation failed
409 Email already registered

request.description:
Logs in with the USER account from `{{userEmail}}` / `{{userPassword}}`.

**Authentication:** none (public). **Role:** any.

**Body (JSON)**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | Non-empty; matched case-insensitively |
| `password` | string | yes | Non-empty |

On success the response sets two HttpOnly cookies, `accessToken` (path `/`) and `refreshToken` (path `/api/auth`). The body contains the user only; tokens are never returned in the body. Postman stores the cookies and sends them with later requests automatically.

Logging in replaces any cookies from a previous login (for example the ADMIN's).

**Script:** stores `data.user.id` in `{{userId}}`.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Logged in, cookies set |
| `400` | `Validation failed`: email or password missing |
| `401` | `Invalid email or password` (same response for an unknown email and a wrong password) |

request.description:
Same endpoint as *Login (USER)*, using the seeded admin account `{{adminEmail}}` / `{{adminPassword}}`.

**Authentication:** none (public).

ADMIN accounts cannot be registered through the API. Create one once with `npm run seed:admin` in `backend/` (reads `SEED_ADMIN_NAME`, `SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `backend/.env`), then set the `adminEmail` and `adminPassword` collection variables to match.

Running this replaces the USER's cookies in Postman's cookie jar; run *Login (USER)* again to switch back.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Logged in as ADMIN, cookies set |
| `400` | Email or password missing |
| `401` | `Invalid email or password` (check the admin variables and that the seed script ran) |

request.description:
Returns the user behind the current `accessToken` cookie. Useful to check who is logged in.

**Authentication:** required (`accessToken` cookie). **Role:** any.

The returned user has only `id`, `name`, `email` and `role`.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Logged in |
| `401` | `Authentication required` (no cookie), `Invalid or expired access token`, `Session is no longer valid` (logged out or refreshed), or `User no longer exists` |

Issues a new access token and a new refresh token from the `refreshToken` cookie. Use it when protected calls start returning `401` because the 15-minute access token expired.

**Authentication:** the `refreshToken` cookie (path `/api/auth`); no access token needed. **Body:** none.

The session is **rotated**: the old refresh token is revoked and works only once, so running this twice with the same cookie fails the second time. Postman stores the new cookies automatically, so consecutive runs in Postman succeed.

On failure the cookies are left unchanged; log in again.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | New cookies set, body contains the user |
| `401` | `Refresh token required` (no cookie) or `Invalid or expired refresh token` (unknown, expired, already used, or logged out) |

request.description:
Revokes the session behind the `refreshToken` cookie and clears both cookies. The access token stops working immediately (every protected call checks the session).

**Authentication:** not required; it works even when the access token has already expired, or with no cookies at all. **Body:** none.

Only the current session (device) is logged out; other logins of the same user stay active.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Always |

item.name: Service Requests
item.description:
Service requests (`/api/requests`). **Every endpoint requires a logged-in user** (the `accessToken` cookie); without it the API returns `401`.

## Who can do what

| Action | USER | ADMIN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | Yes (becomes the owner) | No, `403` |
| List | Only their own | All requests |
| Get by ID | Only their own; another user's request returns `404` | Any request |
| Update fields | Only their own, only while `PENDING` (else `409`) | No, `403` |
| Cancel (`DELETE`) | Only their own, while `PENDING` or `IN_PROGRESS` (else `409`) | No, `403` |
| Change status | No, `403` | Any request, following the workflow |

Roles are checked by the route (`403`). Ownership is checked in the service and reported as `404 Request not found`, exactly as for a missing request, so a USER cannot discover other users' request ids.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | Trimmed, 3–100 characters |
| `description` | string | Trimmed, 10–2000 characters |
| `category` | string | One of `TECHNICAL`, `BILLING`, `ACCOUNT`, `OTHER` |
| `priority` | string | Optional. One of `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` (default `MEDIUM`) |

`status` always starts as `PENDING` and **cannot** be set on create or update (it is ignored). It changes only through *Cancel request* (USER) or *Update request status* (ADMIN). `createdBy` is taken from the logged-in user; a `createdBy` sent in the body is ignored.

## Status workflow

```
PENDING ──► IN_PROGRESS ──► RESOLVED   (final)
   │             │
   └─────────────┴────────► CANCELLED  (final)
```

| From | Allowed next statuses |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | `IN_PROGRESS`, `CANCELLED` |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `RESOLVED` | none (final) |
| `CANCELLED` | none (final) |

Any other change, including a "change" to the same status (e.g. `PENDING` → `PENDING`), returns `409 Cannot change status from X to Y`.

## Common errors

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `Validation failed` (`errors` per field), `Invalid ID` (`:id` is not an ObjectId), `Malformed JSON` |
| `401` | Not logged in, or the access token/session is no longer valid |
| `403` | Role not allowed for this endpoint |
| `404` | Request does not exist, or belongs to another USER |
| `409` | Status rule violated |

request.description:
Creates a service request owned by the logged-in USER. The new request always starts as `PENDING`.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `USER` only (an ADMIN gets `403`).

**Body (JSON)**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | yes | Trimmed, 3–100 characters |
| `description` | string | yes | Trimmed, 10–2000 characters |
| `category` | string | yes | `TECHNICAL`, `BILLING`, `ACCOUNT` or `OTHER` |
| `priority` | string | no | `LOW`, `MEDIUM` or `HIGH`; defaults to `MEDIUM` |

Do not send `status` or `createdBy`: they are controlled by the backend and ignored if present.

The response returns `createdBy` as the owner's id (not populated).

**Script:** stores `data.request._id` in `{{requestId}}`.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `201` | Created |
| `400` | `Validation failed` (`errors` lists each invalid field) or `Malformed JSON` |
| `401` | Not logged in |
| `403` | Logged in as ADMIN |

response.name: 201 Created
400 Validation failed
403 ADMIN cannot create requests

query.description: Optional. Case-insensitive literal match anywhere in `title` or `description`. Empty/whitespace means no search.

request.description:
Lists service requests with pagination, filters, search and sorting.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `USER` or `ADMIN`.

- A **USER** only ever sees their own requests, whatever the filters say.
- An **ADMIN** sees every request.

**Query parameters** (all optional; enable the ones you need in the *Params* tab)

| Parameter | Default | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `1` | Whole number ≥ 1 |
| `limit` | `10` | Whole number 1–50 |
| `status` | none | `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `category` | none | `TECHNICAL`, `BILLING`, `ACCOUNT`, `OTHER` |
| `priority` | none | `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` |
| `search` | none | Case-insensitive, literal match in `title` or `description` |
| `sortBy` | `createdAt` | `createdAt` or `updatedAt` |
| `order` | `desc` | `asc` or `desc` |

An invalid value (e.g. `page=abc`, `limit=51`, `status=` empty, or a parameter repeated twice) returns `400` listing every bad parameter; it is never replaced by the default. Unknown parameters are ignored.

`data` is the array of requests with `createdBy` populated as `{ name, email, id }`. `pagination.total` counts all matching requests; `totalPages` is `ceil(total / limit)` (`0` when nothing matches). A page past the end returns an empty array.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `400` | `Validation failed` for a query parameter |
| `401` | Not logged in |

request.description:
Partially updates the content of the logged-in USER's own request. Only allowed while the request is `PENDING`.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `USER` only (an ADMIN gets `403`).

**Path parameters:** `id`, the request `_id` (defaults to `{{requestId}}`).

**Body (JSON):** any of the fields below; send only the ones you change, but **at least one** is required.

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | string | Trimmed, 3–100 characters |
| `description` | string | Trimmed, 10–2000 characters |
| `category` | string | One of `TECHNICAL`, `BILLING`, `ACCOUNT`, `OTHER` |
| `priority` | string | Optional. One of `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH` (default `MEDIUM`) |

`status` cannot be changed here (it is ignored); use *Cancel request* or the ADMIN status endpoint. A body containing only `status` is rejected with `400 At least one field is required`.

The response returns `createdBy` as the owner's id (not populated).

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Updated |
| `400` | `At least one field is required`, `Validation failed` (`errors` per field), `Invalid ID`, or `Malformed JSON` |
| `401` | Not logged in |
| `403` | Logged in as ADMIN |
| `404` | `Request not found`: no such request, or it belongs to another USER |
| `409` | `Only pending requests can be edited` (status is `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED` or `CANCELLED`) |

request.description:
Cancels the logged-in USER's own request by setting its status to `CANCELLED`. Despite the `DELETE` method, **nothing is deleted**: the request stays in the history and is returned in the response.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `USER` only (an ADMIN gets `403`; admins cancel through *Update request status*).

**Path parameters:** `id`, the request `_id` (defaults to `{{requestId}}`). **Body:** none.

Allowed from `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS`. `RESOLVED` and `CANCELLED` are final, so cancelling them returns `409`.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Cancelled; `data.request.status` is `CANCELLED` |
| `400` | `Invalid ID` |
| `401` | Not logged in |
| `403` | Logged in as ADMIN |
| `404` | `Request not found`: no such request, or it belongs to another USER |
| `409` | `Cannot change status from RESOLVED to CANCELLED` / `from CANCELLED to CANCELLED` |

request.description:
Moves any request to its next status, following the workflow.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `ADMIN` only (a USER gets `403`). Run *Authentication › Login (ADMIN)* first.

**Path parameters:** `id`, the request `_id` (defaults to `{{requestId}}`).

**Body (JSON)**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | yes | `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `RESOLVED` or `CANCELLED`, **and** allowed from the current status |

**Valid transitions**

```
PENDING ──► IN_PROGRESS ──► RESOLVED   (final)
   │             │
   └─────────────┴────────► CANCELLED  (final)
```

| From | Allowed next statuses |
| --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | `IN_PROGRESS`, `CANCELLED` |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | `RESOLVED`, `CANCELLED` |
| `RESOLVED` | none (final) |
| `CANCELLED` | none (final) |

Any other change, including a "change" to the same status (e.g. `PENDING` → `PENDING`), returns `409 Cannot change status from X to Y`.

The body is validated before the request is looked up, so an invalid `status` value returns `400` even for an unknown id.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Status changed |
| `400` | `Validation failed` (`status` missing or not one of the four values), `Invalid ID`, or `Malformed JSON` |
| `401` | Not logged in |
| `403` | Logged in as USER |
| `404` | `Request not found` |
| `409` | `Cannot change status from X to Y`: transition not allowed (including same status, and anything from `RESOLVED`/`CANCELLED`) |

item.name: Users / Admin
item.description:
Admin-only user management (`/api/users`).

`GET /api/users` is currently the only endpoint under `/api/users`. There are no endpoints to view, update, delete or change the role of a single user. ADMIN-only request operations (status changes) are in the *Service Requests* folder.

Run *Authentication › Login (ADMIN)* before these requests.

request.description:
Lists every user (USERs and ADMINs), newest first. No pagination, filters or query parameters.

**Authentication:** required. **Role:** `ADMIN` only.

Each user has `id`, `name`, `email`, `role`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`; password hashes are never returned.

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | OK |
| `401` | Not logged in |
| `403` | Logged in as USER |

response.name: 403 USER cannot list users

item.name: Health
item.description: Service health check (`/api/health`). Public; no cookies needed.

request.description:
Confirms that the API process is running. It does not check the database.
